bib.title: Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning, Appendix A. Data Sets (pp. 677-683)

question: Which data sets does the book use to illustrate its algorithms, and how were they built?

results.claim: MNIST digits: 60,000 training and 10,000 test examples.
results.setup: MNIST (LeCun et al., 1998), subset of NIST data modified
results.quote:
It com-
prises a training set of 60, 000 examples and a test set of 10, 000 examples.
results.note: Printed with spaces, '60, 000' and '10, 000'; the quote keeps that spacing.

results.claim: MNIST images are size-normalized to a 20x20 box then centred in 28x28; grey scale from anti-aliasing.
results.quote:
These images were then
centred in a 28 × 28 box.

results.claim: MNIST test error rates quoted: 12% simple linear classifier, 0.56% SVM, 0.4% convolutional network.
results.setup: Error rates cited from LeCun et al. 1998 (1998-era results, not Bishop's own runs)
results.quote: Error rates for classifying the digits range from 12% for a simple linear classi-
results.note: Dated: modern CNNs are well below 0.4%.

results.claim: Oil flow: synthetic, 12-dimensional observations (6 dual-energy gamma beams), 1,000 points each in train, validation and test sets.
results.setup: Bishop and James (1993); integration time 10 s; 3 phase configurations (homogeneous, annular, laminar/stratified)
results.quote:
The data set is divided into training, validation, and test sets, each of which
comprises 1, 000 independent data points.
results.note: Each point = 12 path lengths + oil and water fractions + binary label for configuration.

results.claim: Oil flow integration time is 10 seconds, chosen as typical of a practical setup.
results.quote:
with a speciﬁc choice of integration time (10 seconds) chosen as characteristic of a
typical practical setup.

results.claim: Old Faithful: 272 observations of eruption duration and time to next eruption, both in minutes.
results.quote:
The data set comprises 272 observations, each of which represents a single erup-
tion
results.note: Provenance of the measurements is not given; only 'several other data sets' remark.

results.claim: Synthetic regression data: x uniform on (0,1), t = sin(2 pi x) plus Gaussian noise with standard deviation 0.3; sample size varies by use in the book.
results.quote:
then adding random noise with
a Gaussian distribution having standard deviation 0.3.

results.claim: Synthetic classification data: two classes with equal priors, one class a single Gaussian and the other a mixture of two Gaussians, so true posteriors and optimal boundary are computable.
results.quote:
The second data set is a classiﬁcation problem having two classes, with equal
prior probabilities

limits: Gives no sample sizes for the synthetic sets, no Gaussian parameters for the classification set, and no provenance (collection date, licence) for Old Faithful.
Data files and formats are on the book web site (http://research.microsoft.com/~cmbishop/PRML), not in the appendix; that URL is likely dead.

terms.definition: Synthetic data from dual-energy gamma densitometry of oil, water and gas phases in a pipe; 12-dimensional inputs, 3 phase configurations

figures.caption: The three geometrical configurations of the oil, water, and gas phases used to generate the oil-flow data set.
figures.why: Shows homogeneous, stratified, annular layouts at a glance

figures.caption: Synthetic classification data set with true posterior probabilities and optimal decision boundary.
